messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: region=us-west-2 gateway_rate_5xx spike detected (90th=14%, p50 latency 1.9s) — auto-page sent to oncall.

matt: oncall here, seeing the page. quick check: are all customer-facing pools affected or just gateway edges?

jia: i'm on it — initial dashboard shows 502s from our egress NATs to backend model-hosting clusters. Errors started ~ 1714999800, sharp jump at 1714999940.

sofia: what pattern do we see? connection resets or long tails?

jia: mostly connection resets and TLS handshakes failing. tcp retransmits high. looks like SNAT port exhaustion on the NAT gateways in the us-west-2 tenant VPCs.

matt: ok, that would explain widespread 502/timeouts. did any deploys hit region around that time? deploy bot?

pagerduty-bot: matt acknowledged the page.

sofia: checked deploys: no production deploys in the last hour for gateway or model-worker. infra autoscaler changed nothing.

eli: i can run quick probe from edge nodes — running `curl -v https://model-hosting-usw2.internal/health` from a couple of proxies now.

eli: (logs) `* Connected to model-hosting-usw2.internal (10.8.3.21) port 443 (#0)` then `* TLS handshake: unexpected EOF` then `curl: (35) error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number` — intermittent.

matt: thanks. if it's SNAT exhaustion, short-term mitigation: expand ephemeral port pool on NATs or fail traffic to a sibling region. let's escalate to ops-lead for capacity change.

ops-lead: noted. i can spin up additional NAT instances and update iptables SNAT range, but that takes ~5-10m for infra changes and region-wide regen risk. alternative: execute controlled traffic steer to us-east-1 for non-low-latency customers.

jia: recommended plan (brief): 1) immediate: bump NAT pool capacity (scale NAT gw + increase ephemeral ports) 2) parallel: roll traffic-shift rule to route non-SLA customers to us-east-1 3) if step1 insufficient, promote read-only fallback for model-hosting in us-east for all failover-capable tenants.

matt: classify customer impact. are PLG customers impacted? enterprise tenants with dedicated VPCs?

jia: majority of errors seen from shared-hosting prefix — PLG and small tenants. Dedicated VPCs show partial errors where egress is via shared NATs. Priority: PLG webhooks, streaming sessions are degraded.

sofia: mark incident SEV=2 (partial outage impacting a subset of customers). we need status page update and pager rotation.

status-bot: Created incident INC-2026-579 (SEV2) — status page draft at /status/incidents/INC-2026-579.

matt: ops-lead please execute NAT scale now. eli coordinate with infra to run quick smoke tests. i'll prepare customer comms draft. jia, ready to apply traffic-shift?

ops-lead: executing: `terraform apply -var region=us-west-2 -target=module.nat_gateway["us-west-2"].scale_up` — applying change. ETA 6m.

(ops logs) ops-lead: NAT instances scaling up, attaching additional EIPs, updating iptables ephemeral port range to 32768-61000.

eli: running smoke: `for i in {1..50}; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://model-hosting-usw2.internal/health || echo fail; done` — initial run: 20x 502/0, now after NAT attach 1x 502, mostly 200.

jia: good signal. continue monitoring 5xx rate. if it drops under 1% for 5m, de-escalate traffic-shift.

matt: ops-lead, leave temporary scale up for 30m. set autoscale policy to add 1 extra NAT if p95 5xx > 3% for >5m.

ops-lead: done. autoscale rule created and andru (infra) pulled.

sofia: while NATs come up, let's pre-stage a traffic-shift: create route policy `traffic-controller set-route --from us-west-2 --to us-east-1 --subset non-sla --weight 100 --dry-run`

jia: dry-run shows safe route, no IP overlap. i'm ready to flip if we see >5% 5xx persist.

status-bot: Status page updated: "Investigating — partial service degradation in us-west-2 affecting some customers (502 errors)."

matt: customer comms draft: "We are investigating increased 502s and timeouts in us-west-2 caused by egress capacity issues; mitigation in progress. No customer data loss. Engineers are scaling infrastructure and routing some traffic to alternate regions. We will update in 30m." anyone edit?

eli: lgtm. add note for customers using private VPCs that they might see delayed webhook deliveries if their egress routes through shared NATs.

ops-lead: NAT capacity scaled, ephemeral ports range extended, 5xx dropped from 13% -> 0.9% in the last 4 minutes. keeping monitoring.`

matt: great. hold on escalation. jia keep the traffic-shift prepped but do not execute. we want to avoid cross-region chatter unless necessary.

jia: acknowledged. traffic-controller in dry-run; will only flip on explicit command if metrics don't stabilize in next 10m.

sofia: verify long-lived streams and streaming clients — some connections may need reconnects because their sockets hit resets. schedule automatic retries in the client SDK to backoff and reconnect. ops note added to incident timeline.

matt: timeline note: 1714999800 first spike, 1714999940 surge, 1715000060 page, 1715000300 NAT scale initiated, 1715000480 error rate fell under 1%.

status-bot: Next update scheduled in 30 minutes.

eli: follow-up tests: `kubectl logs -n gateway gateway-proxy-7f8c | grep "502" | tail -n 5` shows handoffs to us-east-1 for a small fraction (0.2%) due to earlier retries.

matt: can we capture affected customer IDs to proactively message if they had repeated failures?

jia: yes exporting request logs now: `bigquery query --dataset=prod_logs 'SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM requests WHERE region="us-west-2" AND status>=500 AND ts BETWEEN 1714999800 AND 1715000600 GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 50'` — will attach CSV.

ops-lead: recommending postmortem actions: 1) increase default NAT ephemeral ports across shared-hosting by 20% 2) add alert for SNAT port exhaustion metric 3) improve autoscale to pre-warm NATs on sudden p95 load.

sofia: agree. also add client library guidance for reconnect/backoff and document fallback policies for critical tenants.

matt: after-action: if 5xx remains <1% for 30m, we'll close the active page and move to follow-up PM. who owns postmortem? jia?

jia: i'll own postmortem, will include timeline, logs, mitigation steps, and customer impact CSV.

status-bot: Incident INC-2026-579 status updated: "Mitigated — 5xx rates reduced, monitoring. Postmortem assigned to jia."

matt: thanks everyone. quick checklist for next 24h: keep NAT scale elevated for 2h, monitor rollback triggers, prepare customer emails for top 20 affected tenants, schedule postmortem doc by tomorrow EOD.

eli: will follow up with logs and CSV attached in the incident thread.

matt: closing notes: good rapid coord — ops-lead, jia, sofia, eli — stand down but stay reachable.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-579 transitioned to MONITORING by matt at 1715003600.
